atoms.a: Which continent do you think Afrobeats originally comes from?

feedback.end: Afrobeats refers to pop music from West Africa, which has fused with other styles of music to create a sound that is very popular in the UK.

instruction.text: Draw a line between London and Lagos to discover the story behind how Afrobeats started.

end.text: Afrobeats can be traced back to the Afrobeat movement led by the musician Fela Kuti in Nigeria during the sixties and seventies.
end.sound: Afrobeats can be traced back to the Afrobeat movement led by the musician Fella Ckootee in Nigeria during the sixties and seventies.

atoms.b: The sound of Fela Kuti’s Afrobeat ((++movement wave)) was shaped by a mixture of blues, jazz, funk and traditional Nigerian music called Yoruba.
atoms.sound: The sound of Fella Ckootee’s Afrobeat movement was shaped by a mixture of blues, jazz, funk and traditional Nigerian music called Yoruba.

atoms.b: Kuti’s band used a large variety of ((++instruments books)), such as saxophones, drums and guitars.
The lyrics of his songs were often very political. He used his ((++music theatre)) to challenge the Nigerian government and fight for freedom.
Young black musicians today use the lyrics of ((++Afrobeats Eurobeats)) songs similarly to express themselves and uplift their communities.

instruction.text: Select Fela Kuti to hear a sample of early Afrobeat.
Which instrument could you hear in the sample?

feedback.end: The driving rhythm of the drums is an important element of Afrobeat and is also used in modern Afrobeats songs.

instruction.text: Afrobeats as we know it today is a fusion of different musical styles mixed with traditional Afrobeat. Drag the styles of music to the mixing pot.
Select the three ways that most people listen to Afrobeats today.

feedback.correct1: Afrobeats radio stations gave a big platform to Afrobeats when it was first becoming popular in the 2000s.
feedback.correct2: Afrobeats is played at clubs across the country and is connected to lots of dance trends.
feedback.correct3: Afrobeats songs receive billions of listens every year on different music apps because of their danceable rhythms.
